take_homes: Having the tool is not the same as people using it. Handing over the agent file gets you a shell that people quietly stop using.
Pick by the result the person needs to move, not by what fits our platform. Ask what would have to be true for them to drop what they use today.
Write the people plan with owners named. Any role I can't name is an open question, and I should say so.

monday.move: Ask my controller how she writes the month-end variance commentary today, how long it takes, and what a better close would look like. I won't mention a tool. I'll write down one thing that would have to be true for her to switch.
monday.when: Monday morning, now that the October close is done
monday.stop_condition: If she can't give me a time or quality figure I can check, or if IT and legal won't clear finance data for the tool, I drop it.
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data. GDPR and where the data is hosted are also unanswered.

misconception.why: The module says the value sits in the owner's memory and corrections, and a handed-over tool is a shell. That is not what I'd call a licence. But it never gave a cost, payback or per-person figure, so I still half think of it as something you buy and then have to make people use.

one_line: Good warning that buying the tool is not the same as people using it, but it never once told me what it costs or what it pays back.
